comparator.sourceNotes: The official prospective year pages sum to 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one consists of 60 EC compulsory sociology, social problems, survey research, statistics, policy and professional development; zero-credit RADAr is omitted. Year two has 42 EC compulsory theory, lifestyle, statistics, regression, measurement, social research and professional development; 12 EC restricted sociology electives chosen as the first two 6-EC items in published order; and 6 EC genuinely free choice. The alternative Diversities in Care comprises two inseparable 5+1 EC units, and is not counted on this route. Year three has 26 EC compulsory theory/methods/professional development, 12 EC free choice, a compulsory 13-EC labour-market internship and a 9-EC bachelor thesis. The 18 EC free choice across years two and three is left open. These pages are indicative and do not guarantee individual course availability in a future entrant cohort.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two coherent, independently evidenced UCR schedules are feasible and differ in social-science emphasis and at least four courses. A third distinct programme would require an unsupported standalone specialization in demography, migration, family studies or sociology fieldwork; repackaging adjacent psychology or law modules would duplicate the two supported directions.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce sociological perspectives on social institutions and relationships.
Both develop sociological questions and ways of interpreting social phenomena.
Both analyse inequality and collective responses; UCR centres movements and environmental justice.
Both develop contemporary sociological theory; UCR includes different theorists and themes.
Both connect culture/media to social difference; UCR centres racial representation.
No single UCR course covers this specific sociology of household decisions at the same scope.
Both address life-course change, with UCR approaching it through developmental psychology.
Related UCR sociology courses examine institutions and individuals but do not duplicate this micro-macro theory component.
Both teach social inquiry, with UCR focused on qualitative methods.
Both cover descriptive statistics for social research, with UCR spanning business and behavioural examples.
Radboud requires a 9-EC supervised survey research project; related UCR methods courses are not that same credited project.
Both teach inferential quantitative analysis of social/behavioural data.
UCR offers philosophy courses but no single scheduled component equivalent to this social-science philosophy requirement.
UCR statistics touch measurement but do not reproduce the specific scale-construction course.
Both teach regression analysis; UCR econometrics uses economic and social datasets.
Radboud requires a second 9-EC collaborative empirical sociology project; UCR coursework is related but not equivalent.
Both integrate evidence from multiple approaches; UCR focuses on systematic review rather than mixed-method fieldwork.
The required 9-EC independent sociology thesis is not equivalent to ordinary UCR courses.
Both address institutions and justice surrounding crime; UCR gives a broad legal and social introduction rather than a focused sociology of criminality.
Both examine group relations and social influence; UCR approaches these psychologically.
Both examine how evidence relates to public policy; UCR focuses on public economics.
Both develop argument and public communication about contested issues.
Both involve academic and personal development in distinct curricular settings.
Professional and personal development remains a distinct Radboud course.
Both examine political contestation and institutional change; UCR focuses on EU politics.
Both engage climate and inequality, but UCR’s course centres climate science and impacts.
This unrestricted 6-EC course is student-selected; no fixed UCR equivalent is imposed.
Third-year Radboud professional development is a separate credited requirement.
Genuine 12-EC free space remains open to student choice.
The compulsory 13-EC labour-market internship has no same credited UCR placement.

notes.text: Radboud has a continuous disciplinary sociology sequence, successive supervised survey/research projects, a required labour-market internship and a sociology thesis. UCR can build a strong interdisciplinary social-science response but its sociology course set is smaller and the credited project, internship and thesis requirements are not treated as equivalent to ordinary courses.
